headline: Trust Fall Tim Hospitalized After 847th Consecutive Fall Attempt
subheadline: Small Kevin reportedly present at scene; witnesses describe 'déjà vu' of The Incident
summary: Local performance artist Timothy 'Trust Fall Tim' Hendricks is in stable condition after his landmark 847th fall went catastrophically wrong at The Underground.
content:
Timothy Hendricks, known to locals as Trust Fall Tim, was rushed to St. Margaret's Hospital late Saturday evening after what witnesses are calling "a perfect storm of misplaced trust."

The incident occurred at The Underground, where Hendricks was attempting his 847th documented fall - a milestone number he had been celebrating all week on social media. According to venue owner Marcus Chen, the atmosphere was electric.

"Everyone wanted to catch him for lucky 847," Chen recalled. "We had maybe 30 people crowded around. Then Small Kevin pushed to the front."

Small Kevin, whose real name has been withheld, was famously banned from Trust Fall Tim's events following The Incident of March 2022, which resulted in a six-foot drop and concussion. Witnesses report that Kevin had entered through the back and was wearing a fake mustache.

"I saw the mustache come off mid-fall," said attendee Jennifer Observerson, who was at the venue celebrating her recent divorce. "Tim's eyes got so wide. It was like slow motion."

Chen attempted to intervene, managing to grab Tim's left arm while still holding a beer, but the momentum was too great. The fall resulted in a sprained wrist, bruised ego, and what doctors are calling "profound trust-related trauma."

Small Kevin fled the scene and is currently being sought by what one police officer described as "a surprisingly organized vigilante group of regular catchers, led by someone named Big Kevin."

Hendricks' catch rate, previously at an impressive 78.5%, has now dropped to 78.4%. He is expected to make a full recovery and has already posted from his hospital bed: "The trust was always the point. Not the catching. 848 is going to be different."

The Underground has announced enhanced security measures, including a "No Kevins Under 6 Feet" policy.
author: Marcus Webb, Community Affairs Reporter
